proposals: NPCI should publish monthly volume, value and average ticket for every merchant category code it uses, not only the 29 of roughly 300 released so far, so analysis of who pays the new MDR need not rest on categories covering 82 per cent of volume and 52 per cent of value.

NPCI should maintain a public, downloadable month-by-month archive of its merchant-category data, so fee-pool estimates can be built from a full year rather than annualising a single July 2025 snapshot that may miss festival-season spending.

NPCI should publish, from 15 October 2026, the MDR actually collected each month under each tier of the notified schedule — the 0.4 per cent general rate, the flat ₹5 categories and the 0.02 per cent capital-market rate — so the fee’s real burden by category can be checked against these estimates.

NPCI should tag payments routed through delivery platforms and online marketplaces with the underlying merchant’s category as well as the platform’s, so restaurant, fast-food and marketplace-seller volumes are not undercounted when fee exposure is measured.

The Ministry of Finance should publish, alongside the MDR notification, the share of person-to-merchant UPI volume and value that falls under each exemption — tickets of ₹2,000 or less and merchants under ₹1 lakh a month — so the scope of the carve-outs is stated rather than inferred.
